summary: Koshu Sato is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1997 and held a researcher post at the Eastern Institute.

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He taught at Osaka University (~1963–1968), Hokkaido University (~1968–1989), and served as president of Sapporo Otani Junior College (~1993–1999).
Kotetsu Yoshida (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as professor emeritus at Taisho University (~1983–2013) and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo until around 1930. He later held an academic post at Taisho University.

Koun Yamada (1907–1989) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at First Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University. He worked at NOF Corporation (~1945–1969) and succeeded Hakuun Yasutani from 1970 to 1989.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Shimizu held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed a master's degree at the University of Tokyo in 1959. He held posts at Nishogakusha University and Toyo University (~1970–2002).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist educated at Calcutta, Oxford, Cotton University, and Sanskrit College. He served as Principal of Jagannath Barooah College (~1930–1934) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1948–1956).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar educated at Hare School and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School (~1828–1832) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (~1852–1867).

Krishnanath Chatterjee specialized in Indology and philosophy. His teachers included Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amareshwar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She served as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary (~2006–2019) and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She held posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College (~2006–2008).

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She completed her doctoral candidacy and worked as an editor at Lund University (~2002–2007), later becoming an assistant professor at Linnaeus University in 2011.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) specialized in Sinology and religious studies, studying at the EPHE, Paris's Faculty of Arts, and INALCO. He held posts at École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1970) and Leiden University (~1993–1999).

Krisztina Teleki (b. 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow around 2009.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned her PhD from the University of Calcutta by 1966.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) studied Indology and linguistics at Presidency University, Calcutta, and Allahabad. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (~1923–1956), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1956–1966), and the University of Calcutta.

K. L. Dhammajoti (b. 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He held positions at Kelaniya, Calgary, Hong Kong, and International Buddhist College.

Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge, and served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Ceylon (~1951–1963).

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University. He held posts at Tokyo University of Literature and Science, Japan Women's University, the University of Tokyo, and Komazawa University.
